extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent prosecutors, and patent owners/attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and examiner form-paragraph guidance for drafting, filing, accepting, correcting, withdrawing, and otherwise processing terminal disclaimers in U.S. patent prosecution and reexamination (including signature/capacity, chain-of-title, fee, and procedural requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of acceptable terminal disclaimer language
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample text disclaiming the terminal part of the statutory term of any patent granted on the instant application (or patent) that would extend beyond the expiration date of the full statutory term of a patent granted on a pending reference application or reference patent, and waiver language that the applicant/patentee "waives the right to separately enforce" the instant and reference patents and that the waiver "runs with" the patent and binds successors or assigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple full-form example paragraphs are provided (for provisional nonstatutory double patenting over a pending application; for nonstatutory double patenting over a reference patent; and reexamination situations). Examiner notes direct examiners to use specified form paragraphs for joint research agreement situations (14.27.07.fti / 14.27.07.1) or other situations (14.27.04.fti / 14.27.04.1 and 14.27.06).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer must be signed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.321(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer must be signed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.321(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing date of the application determines which form should be used. An eTerminal Disclaimer filled out online that meets all requirements is auto-processed and approved immediately upon submission. Examiner note: filing the terminal disclaimer by itself is not a complete reply to a nonstatutory double patenting rejection — it must be accompanied by a reply requesting reconsideration of the prior Office action (see MPEP § 804 I.B.1 and 37 CFR 1.111/1.113).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer filing is not a complete reply to an NSDP rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a terminal disclaimer by itself is not a complete reply to a nonstatutory double patenting (NSDP) rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete reply requires that the terminal disclaimer be accompanied by a reply requesting reconsideration of the prior Office action. Even when the NSDP rejection is provisional, the reply must be complete. See MPEP § 804 subsection I.B.1; for replies see 37 CFR 1.111(a) (non-final) and 37 CFR 1.113(c) (final). A request for reconsideration may be filed after final for consideration (see MPEP §§ 706.07(e) and 714.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to state capacity to sign (pre-Sept.16,2012 applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before September 16, 2012, the person who signed the terminal disclaimer must state in what capacity it was signed on behalf of the corporation or other business entity, and the signer must be established as authorized to act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph MUST be preceded by form paragraph 14.24 or 14.25 AND form paragraph 14.26. Do not use this form paragraph in an application filed on or after September 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signer not recognized as officer of assignee (pre-Sept.16,2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the person who signed the terminal disclaimer is not an attorney or agent of record and is not recognized as an officer of the assignee, and has not been established as authorized to act on behalf of the assignee, the terminal disclaimer is defective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph is to be used ONLY in applications filed before September 16, 2012 when the signer is not an authorized officer as defined in MPEP § 324 or is an attorney/agent not of record. MUST be preceded by 14.24 or 14.25 and followed by 14.29.02.fti when appropriate. Use 14.29.02.fti to explain how an official other than a recognized officer may properly sign a terminal disclaimer. An attorney or agent of record is authorized to sign even if not an officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria to accept terminal disclaimer signed by non-recognized officer (pre-Sept.16,2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is acceptable for a person other than a recognized officer to sign a terminal disclaimer provided the record includes a statement that the person is empowered to sign terminal disclaimers and/or act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new terminal disclaimer that includes the empowerment statement will be considered signed by an appropriate official. A separately filed paper referencing the previously filed terminal disclaimer and containing a proper empowerment statement is also acceptable if filed with another copy of the previously filed disclaimer. Examiner notes: MUST be preceded by 14.24 or 14.25 AND 14.29.fti. While indicating the person’s title is desirable, it is not mandatory. Send a sample terminal disclaimer with the Office action to show how to correct the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: No evidence of chain of title to assignee (pre-Sept.16,2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignee has not established its ownership interest in the application (to support the terminal disclaimer) where there is no submission in the record establishing ownership either (a) by providing documentary evidence of a chain of title from the original inventor(s) to the assignee plus a statement affirming that the documentary evidence was or concurrently is being submitted for recordation pursuant to 37 CFR 3.11, or (b) by specifying (by reel and frame number) where such documentary evidence is recorded in the Office (37 CFR 3.73).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph MUST be preceded by form paragraph 14.24 or 14.25. Where an attorney or agent of record signs a terminal disclaimer, there is no need to provide a statement under 37 CFR 3.73. Documentary evidence may be found in the terminal disclaimer itself or in a separate paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: No evidence of chain of title to assignee (reexamination situations)
rubrics_metrics.description: In reexamination, the assignee must establish ownership interest in the patent to support a terminal disclaimer by either: (a) documentary evidence of chain of title from the original inventor(s) to the assignee and a statement that the documentary evidence was or is being submitted for recordation under 37 CFR 3.11; or (b) specifying reel/frame where the chain is recorded in the Office (37 CFR 3.73).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preceding form paragraph requirements apply (MUST be preceded by 14.24 or 14.25). Documentary evidence may be in the terminal disclaimer or a separate paper in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission establishing ownership not signed by appropriate party (pre-Sept.16,2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the submission establishing the assignee's ownership interest is informal or not signed by a person authorized to sign the submission (37 CFR 3.73), the terminal disclaimer is not entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph MUST be preceded by 14.24 or 14.25. Follow this paragraph with one of form paragraphs 14.16.02 or 14.16.03. If neither applies, follow with a detailed statement of why there is no authorization. Use form paragraph 14.16.06 to point out one way to correct the problem. Do not use in applications filed on or after September 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application/patent basis for double patenting rejection must be identified
rubrics_metrics.description: The application or patent which forms the basis for the double patenting rejection must be identified in the terminal disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph when no information is presented. If incorrect information is contained in the terminal disclaimer, use form paragraphs 14.26 and 14.26.05. MUST be preceded by form paragraph 14.24 or 14.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 3.73 — establishing right of assignee to take action (post- and pre-AIA statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 3.73 prescribes how an assignee establishes ownership to take action in patent matters: (b)/(c) ownership is established by a signed statement identifying the assignee, accompanied by either (1) documentary evidence of chain of title (e.g., executed assignment) (with required affirming statement for recordation for patents), or (2) a statement specifying where such documentary evidence is recorded (reel/frame). The original applicant is presumed owner unless there is an assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics include: (c)(2) if an assignee is less than the entire right, the Office may refuse acceptance unless each assignee establishes its ownership percentage or all parties jointly identify owners accounting for entire right; conflicting statements from multiple purported assignees will be resolved by the Director; paragraph (d) requires the submission to show the signer is authorized either by (1) including a statement that the person is authorized to act on behalf of the assignee, (2) being signed by a person with apparent authority, or (3) for patent matters only, being signed by a practitioner of record. The MPEP also provides the pre-AIA version of 37 CFR 3.73 with like requirements and timing (ownership must be submitted prior to or with the paper requesting/taking action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for statement to record assignment submitted with terminal disclaimer (37 CFR 3.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment document submitted as documentary evidence required by 37 CFR 3.73 must be accompanied by a statement affirming that the documentary evidence of the chain of title from the original owner to the assignee was, or concurrently is being, submitted for recordation pursuant to 37 CFR 3.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the assignment document is not accompanied by the required statement and has not been recorded in the Office assignment records, notify applicant using the appropriate form paragraph and insert the file date of the assignment in the Office action. Examiner note: this paragraph should be used when an assignment (original, facsimile, or copy) submitted to satisfy 3.73 was not accompanied by the affirming statement and has not been recorded among assignment records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously submitted disclaimer fee can be applied; pay difference if fee increased
rubrics_metrics.description: A previously paid terminal disclaimer fee (37 CFR 1.20(d)) can be applied when submitting a replacement or supplemental terminal disclaimer; if the fee has increased since previously paid, the applicant/patent owner must pay the difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 14.35 for applicants, 14.35.01 for patent owners. Examiner note: notify applicant/patent owner that the previously submitted fee can be applied when a replacement/supplemental terminal disclaimer is submitted. If fee was increased, pay difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion that applicant/patent owner request a refund when duplicate fee paid
rubrics_metrics.description: If a previously paid disclaimer fee has been applied to a replacement or supplemental terminal disclaimer and another terminal disclaimer fee was paid, applicant/patent owner may request a refund of any payment in excess of the required fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request a refund submit a written request and a copy of the Office action to Mail Stop 16, Director of the USPTO, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450. Note: if applicant/patent owner authorized a refund to be credited to a deposit account or credit card, appropriate credit should be made and this paragraph should NOT be used. Use 14.36 for applicant, 14.36.01 for patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO terminal disclaimer forms and eTerminal availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO website contains terminal disclaimer forms to overcome provisional NSDP rejections over pending applications or reference patents; the filing date of the application determines which form to use. An eTerminal Disclaimer may be filled out online and, if it meets requirements, is auto-processed and approved immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner note: include reference to www.uspto.gov/PatentForms and www.uspto.gov/TerminalDisclaimer for more information. Use the form appropriate for the filing date; eTerminal streamlines processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of a recorded terminal disclaimer before issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: A recorded terminal disclaimer may be withdrawn if a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 is granted before the application in which it is filed issues as a patent, or if filed in a reexamination proceeding, before the reexamination certificate issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under appropriate circumstances the nullification of an erroneously filed recorded terminal disclaimer may be addressed by filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.182. Petitions seeking to reopen the propriety of the underlying double patenting rejection have not been favorably considered. Filing a continuing application other than a CPA, while abandoning the application containing the terminal disclaimer, will typically nullify the effect of the terminal disclaimer. Filing an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 will not nullify the effect because prosecution is continued in the existing application rather than filing a new one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recorded terminal disclaimer cannot be nullified after patent or reexamination certificate issues
rubrics_metrics.description: After a patent or reexamination certificate issues, a recorded terminal disclaimer will not be nullified; mechanisms to correct patents (certificate of correction, reissue, reexamination, IPR, PGR, CBM) are not available to withdraw or nullify the effect of a recorded terminal disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public policy disfavors restoring to the patent owner what was dedicated to the public. Certificate of Correction (35 U.S.C. 255) is limited to clerical/typographical/minor mistakes and corrections that do not constitute new matter or require reexamination. Reissue (35 U.S.C. 251) cannot be used to withdraw a terminal disclaimer because reissue cannot extend the unexpired part of the original patent term and recapture principles bar restoring disclaimed term. Case law cited: In re Jentoft; Altoona Publix Theatres v. American Tri-Ergon Corp.; In re Yamazaki; Ball Corp. v. United States; Ex parte Anthony; In re Dinsmore. Also nullification would improperly enlarge the vertical scope of claims (Board remarks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of errors in naming patent owner(s) after issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recorded terminal disclaimer has an error in the naming of the patent owner(s) or applicant, the patent owner may file a paper explaining the error(s) and requesting that the explanation be included in the file history, and may file additional terminal disclaimers naming the correct owner(s) accompanied by the fee(s) for processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper requesting acknowledgment may be filed and the Office can add the explanation to the file history. Filing additional terminal disclaimers naming correct owners with fees will be processed by the Office.
